beats.spoken: Nobody checks cosmetics before they go on sale. That's not true.

Article 3 of the EU cosmetics regulation says a cosmetic must be safe for human health when used under normal or reasonably foreseeable conditions. That's the basic duty. Presentation, labelling, instructions and warnings all count towards that.

How is that shown? Before a product goes on the market, the responsible person must make sure it has been through a safety assessment and that a safety report exists. New information after launch goes into the report.
And not just anyone can do it. The safety assessment is carried out by a person with a university qualification in pharmacy, toxicology, medicine or a similar subject.

In the US, the law doesn't prescribe specific tests. But since MoCRA, the responsible person has to keep records that adequately support the safety of their products. Animal testing isn't required there to market a cosmetic.
So cosmetics are checked before sale. Not by an authority issuing an approval, but through a qualified assessment that the responsible person stands behind.
